chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād al-Nāb, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who does not know whether he has prayed the fajr prayer as two rakʿahs or one rakʿah. He said: He should recite the tashahhud and depart, then stand and pray one rakʿah. If he had already prayed two rakʿahs, then this would be supererogatory; and if he had prayed one rakʿah, then this would complete the prayer. And this, by Allah, is from that which is never made up.

So this is an anomalous report, contrary to all the other reports, and the sect has agreed upon leaving action according to it. However, it is possible that the doubt concerned the two supererogatory rakʿahs of fajr, so it was permissible for him to build upon one and pray another rakʿah as a precaution. There is no mention of the obligatory prayer in the report; rather, it mentions the fajr prayer, and that expression may be used for both the obligatory and the sunnah prayer. According to this interpretation, it does not contradict the reports previously mentioned.

key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the fajr prayer discussed in the report
key_terms.خَبَرٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report not in agreement with the established reports
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: he recites the tashahhud before ending the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should be done if someone doubts whether they prayed one or two rakʿahs of fajr?
ai.summary: This report discusses a case of doubt regarding whether one has prayed one or two rakʿahs of fajr. The compiler then states that the report is anomalous and not acted upon in its apparent sense, suggesting instead that it may refer to the supererogatory fajr prayer, thereby reconciling it with the other narrations.
